system: Unchanged base weights, B0 typed-decision runtime with 2 to 256 choice options; no trained adapter.
schedule_description: 100 real texts (25 each from CLINC, MTop, GoEmotions and DBpedia) from the published Decision Models Under Pressure v3 rq1 extension pools at revision 21820dc8b455e37aebaf5a83122233b6e564c109. Each text is asked at 16, 32, 64, 128 and 256 options, in the original option order and a second permuted order, three repeats: 1,500 primary plus 1,500 shuffled-order control calls.
accuracy_rule: Highest probability with exact ties broken by option key name; failed or invalid calls count as wrong in the full denominator.

dmup.license: data CC BY-SA 4.0 per the dataset card; repository code is used read-only per its README

sources.wide_reference: none: no published Jev or AutoTrust option-scaling numbers exist for this subset, so this panel has no scoreboard comparison

scope: The 100 texts are reused across option counts, orderings and repeats (3,000 calls, 100 unique items), so this is paired scaling evidence, not 3,000 independent examples.
Compared with our own 16-option results on the same panel, not with any published model; no fresh Jev calls.
Distractor pools come from the published rq1 extension splits; the shuffled ordering is our control, not a published artifact.
Probabilities are normalised raw option logits, not certified calibrated confidence.
Task text, distractor pools and semantic label descriptions are not redistributed. The verifier includes gold option keys alongside item identifiers and our measured outputs.
